title: Material 3: theming, dark mode and dynamic colour

videos.script: Your screen should never ask for green. It should ask for primary, and let the theme decide what primary is. {{roles}} That is what this lesson builds: a theme for the planner. Colours come in pairs. Primary, and on primary for whatever is drawn on it. {{type}} Then type and shape, which work the same way. A screen asks for title medium, and the theme says what that is. {{dark}} Then dark mode. A test asks for night, the way a phone does, and the same screen comes back dark. Not one line of it changed. {{dynamic}} Then dynamic colour, from the wallpaper. This machine has no wallpaper, and the lesson shows what it got instead, and why that is not a capture of anybody's phone. {{contrast}} And last, contrast. Eight colour pairs, each measured against the number accessibility asks for. A test that fails the build if one of them drops.
